title: How this works
lead: Four things worth knowing before you start. Nothing here is required reading.

cards.title: Bands
cards.lead: A document is a vertical stack of bands. Hover a gap in the outline on the left and press + text or + canvas to add one.

rows.text: Text in normal flow: headings, paragraphs, quotes, lists, bold, italic, links and colour.
A free area with its own height. Images, video, embeds and shapes sit wherever you put them.
A canvas band set to overlay takes no height of its own and sits on top of the band above it. That is how a photo ends up beside a paragraph instead of under it.

cards.note: Drag the grip to reorder a band. The first band cannot overlay; there is nothing above it.

rows.text: Resize from that corner. Hold shift to keep the ratio.
Rotate about the centre. Hold shift to snap to 15 degrees.
Blue lines appear when an edge or a centre lines up with something else. Hold alt to ignore them.
Add to or remove from the selection. Drag empty space for a marquee.
Send backward, bring forward. Add cmd for all the way back or front.
Abandon the drag you are in, then clear the selection.
Writes the draft. The draft is stored, but it is not on the live site and visitors cannot reach it. Cmd-S does the same thing.
Copies the draft over the live page. This is the only step that changes what the site shows.
The dot in the top bar. Amber means the last edit is still only in this browser.

cards.title: Preview
cards.lead: Preview saves the draft first, then opens the page drawn by the same renderer the live site uses. What you see is what publishing would give you.

rows.text: As designed. The width the layout is built against.
Phone. Below 900px the canvas stops positioning: items stack in order, full width, and overlay is ignored.

cards.note: Switching width does not reload the page, so you can flip between them quickly.
